publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
title_or_table: Summary of Economic Projections, September 16, 2026: Table 1 (economic projections, unemployment rate) and Table 2 (average historical projection error ranges)
observation_period: Projections made at the September 15 to 16, 2026 meeting for the fourth quarters of 2026 to 2029 and the longer run
universe_or_base: Projections of the civilian unemployment rate, average for the fourth quarter of each year, by Federal Reserve Board members and Reserve Bank presidents under each one's own view of appropriate policy
unit: percent; historical_error is the root mean squared error of past projections in percentage points; band_70_low and band_70_high are the median minus and plus that error, computed by the studio
qualification: Projections are officials' expectations, not forecasts of what will happen. Table 2's note says that under certain assumptions there is about a 70 percent probability that actual outcomes fall within ranges set by past errors (forecasts for 2006 through 2025); the band here applies those errors to the median as the Fed's own fan charts do. The longer run has no error range
printed_source_line: Source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Summary of Economic Projections, September 16, 2026, Tables 1 and 2, unemployment rate projections for 2026 to 2029, United States. Retrieved November 11, 2026. Officials’ projections; the band applies the average error of past forecasts.
